text:
emma: Heads-up — proposing we offload the enrichment pipeline (user metadata + ranking signals) out of the hot runtime. Posting a short plan here for feedback.

raj: +1. The p99 tails are dominated by those enrichment calls. What minimal data contract do we need to keep sync?

emma: Proposal: keep synchronous minimal fields only (req_id, user_id, profile_key). Everything else is async via event stream -> worker. If enrichment missing, runtime uses cached defaults. Sketch: ```{ "req_id": "uuid", "user_id": "uid", "profile_key": "k" }```

carmen: Sounds reasonable. But how do we handle features that must be present for scoring correctness?

emma: Two modes: soft-offload (non-blocking, model degrades gracefully when enrichments are absent) and strict-offload (blocking) behind a feature flag. Start soft by default.

raj: Migration plan? We need canary + circuit-breaker for enrichment latency.

emma: Migration steps: 1) Add enrichment sidecar API + feature flag. 2) Shadow enrichment calls to the new worker (no behavioral change). 3) Canary 5% strict-offload with strict metrics. 4) Ramp and remove hotpath enrichment. 5) Cleanup fallback code after 2 months. Track metrics at each step.

carmen: Metrics to watch: enrichment latency distribution, cache hit rate, model perf delta (AUC/CTR), 503s, and end-to-end p99. Also add synthetic tests that simulate missing enrichments.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment 1768765450 started for enrichment-sidecar v0.3 -> dev cluster :rocket: 

sylvia: Ordering/consistency question: enrichment events might arrive after scoring response — how are we handling late enrichment?

emma: We'll write enrichment events with req_id and TTL. Worker will try to pre-enrich for expected req_id patterns. If enrichment arrives late, we update downstream stores and use it for subsequent requests. For strict sync features we keep the option to block. Not ideal but acceptable for non-blocking features.

raj: Queue/backpressure concerns: we should partition by tenant, use Kafka with retention short TTL, and add per-tenant rate limits to avoid noisy neighbors. Also size the consumer group to match 99th percentile throughput.

carmen: Rollback plan: flip feature flag to route back to hotpath. Keep both code paths for 8 weeks. Alert if strict-offload error rate > 0.5% or model perf drops > 0.5%.

emma: I'll draft a short RFC + PR containing the sidecar interface, the migration runbook, and the canary dashboard query. Assigning @raj to own the canary + dashboard, @carmen to own model-eval before/after.

raj: :thumbsup: Will put together a dashboard (calls/sec, latency p50/95/99, cache hit, model quality deltas).

carmen: Also adding an integration test that runs the model with synthetic enriched vs unenriched inputs to quantify drift.

emma: Thanks — will post the RFC link and PR in this thread when ready.
